title: 45s technical flip brief (seller cheat) - wip
content:
Purpose: a 45-second, technically credible flip for seller-facing conversations that converts engineers/architects from skeptical to curious. Lightweight slide-style brief + speaker notes. NOT a full deck — one-pager seller tool for live calls or booth conversations.

Audience: integration architect, platform engineer, ML infra lead. Assumes 60–90s total from the seller; engineer wants: latency, SLA, deployment modes, and safe fallback.

Slide 1 - TL;DR (the 45s script):
- Opening (10s): 'Redwood gives teams a single runtime for predictable LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — same API, consistent latency targets, and observable cost controls.'
- Proof points (20s): 'We support streaming & tool-calls, dedicated GPU pools with SLA-backed latency, and automatic routing/fallback so apps stay online under load. Customers cut per-token cost via prefix caching and batching; we provide kernel-selection tuned to model + hardware.'
- Close (15s): 'If you care about latency + unit economics and need consistent rollouts across cloud and on-prem, we should run a quick rack-level demo and a 2-week pilot.'

Quick rebut bullets (have these ready, 10–20s each):
- "Why not just host on raw GPUs?" — Ops cost + brittle performance: we provide pre-tuned runtime, autoscaling, and canary rollouts so you avoid capacity blackholes.
- "Open models vary — how do you manage regressions?" — Built-in evals and rollout controls; you pin versions and run small-scale A/B quality checks before promoting.
- "What about compliance / private data?" — Private deployment option with customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM for keys; audit logs surface token-level usage.

Demo prompts (2–3 minute live prompts to use in quick demo):
- Show latency SLO for a 512-token chat convo vs fallback to a quantized variant.
- Toggle routing policy: route to cheaper quantized instance under 95th percentile load; show automatic fallback and error handling.
- Display per-route cost heatmap and token breakdown for a recent trace.

Rapid FAQ snippets (single-line answers for sellers):
- "Is data exfiltration a risk?" — Private deploy + KMS + audit logs minimize risk; hosted has encryption at rest and effacement policies.
- "How do you control cost spikes?" — Autoscale + burst limits + routing to cheaper variants; Optimize suggests quantization and batching changes.
- "Do you support streaming + function calls?" — Yes, full streaming + structured output and tool-calling supported.

Objection handling map (short):
- Concern: cost predictability -> Show reserved capacity options + usage-based plan with burst controls.
- Concern: integration complexity -> Share simple SDK snippet and 15-min integration checklist.

Seller playbook next steps (1–2 lines each):
- Offer a 20-min technical discovery: collect top-3 latency targets and sensitive data requirements.
- Propose a 2-week pilot on Dedicated or Private (small reserved pool) with explicit success criteria (latency P95, token cost delta, and functional parity tests).
- If interested, schedule model-onboarding call with Applied ML + Solutions Eng.

Notes to seller:
- Keep script tight; engineers respect concrete SLOs and a short demo.
- Avoid broad marketing claims — cite specific features (prefix caching, canary rollouts, KMS).
- Use the demo prompts to shift the conversation from feature to measurable outcomes.

Draft checklist before call:
- Confirm target model size and avg sequence length (helps pick demo model).
- Confirm whether customer prefers private or hosted path.
- Pull a recent trace in Console for a live example (if available).

Open questions for internal iteration:
- Do we want a 30s variant aimed at enterprise buyers?
- Can Solutions Eng produce a 2-min recorded demo to attach?

References: short links to internal runbooks and a demo repo (see linked_artifacts).

End of brief. This is intentionally terse — make edits for local region specifics and add any customer anecdotes under the 'live examples' section when moving to final.
